verdicts.note: Makena announced 2 Mar 2010; servers off 11:59 pm PST 9 Mar 2010. Wilson letter quoted: membership and in-world numbers 'continued to grow' while there was 'a marked decrease in revenue, which, in these economic times, is no surprise'. Reopening announced 18 May 2011; reopened to the public 2 May 2012 on a subscription model with two free-trial tiers; US$10/month appears in the Wikipedia summary. Wording of the letter comes from secondary reprints. (Also: https://www.engadget.com/2010/03/02/there-com-is-closing/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There_(virtual_world))

24 Mar 2010: $4.2M from Kolohala Ventures and Henk Rogers; total invested 'more than $13 million' per press release (TechCrunch, GameDeveloper). Engadget 16 Jan 2011: CEO Jim Sink's letter said Avatar Reality was 'dropping PC development for Blue Mars in favor of iOS' and that staff including Sink were let go. Staff of 30 cut to 10 (CB Insights summary; Modem World: 'reduced staffing by two-thirds, to just 10 people'). Caveat: the 30-to-10 figure is secondary and CB Insights mis-attributes the quote to Hashimoto as CEO. (Also: https://www.engadget.com/2011-01-16-second-life-competitor-blue-mars-drops-pc-development-for-apple.html)

Closure confirmed: announced April 2008, servers dark 1 Aug 2008 (GameDeveloper 'EA-Land to close in August', Wikipedia, MassivelyOP). The 105,000 peak is sourced only to thesimsnews.com; another account says the game 'had only about 15,000 active monthly subscribers' by 2003. Correct to: 'about 105,000 subscribers per one fan report, contested; another account gives ~15,000 active subscribers in 2003'. Not an established figure. (Also: https://gamedeveloper.com/game-platforms/-i-ea-land-i-to-close-in-august, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sims_Online)

Sony Japan announced first in Aug 2014 (Asian territories); Western announcement 29 Sept 2014 by Paul Sullivan on the PlayStation Blog citing a 'shifting landscape'; no new content after 12 Nov 2014; downloads off 3 Dec 2014; closed 31 Mar 2015. 41M is the Wikipedia infobox registered-member figure; Sony itself said 'tens of millions of users'; no primary Sony source for 41M surfaced, so the brief's caveat is right. Minor: Western announcement was 29 Sept, not 26 Sept as the earlier checker said. A developer co-founder said Home was profitable but Sony 'wasn't interested in smaller profit margins'. (Also: https://www.techradar.com/news/gaming/the-messy-doomed-journey-of-playstation-home-as-told-by-its-architect-1275149, https://delistedgames.com/?p=2126)

PCWorld (24 Jan 2014) and TechCrunch: team joins Yahoo, service closes 21 Feb 2014, financial terms not disclosed; PCWorld explicitly calls it an acqui-hire and TechCrunch reads it as a small talent acquisition; users were given an export guide. (Also: https://techcrunch.com/2014/01/24/yahoo-acquires-will-shut-down-browser-based-virtual-world-gaming-startup-cloud-party)

Rosedale 'had said in 2013 that 10 or 20 million people would be using HMDs daily by now, but the number is far lower, close to two orders of magnitude below that' (VentureBeat frames it as a 2014 prediction of 'millions' vs actual 'tens of thousands'). May 2019: 25% / 20 employees laid off. 11 Dec 2019: team halved, apps withdrawn from Steam and Oculus stores, HFC cash-outs end after 15 Jan 2020, GitHub repo private 15 Jan 2020, forums/support ended same date. NOT surfaced by search: the $35M June 2018 round and ~$73M total; treat those as prior knowledge (both earlier checkers agree). (Also: https://venturebeat.com/technology/high-fidelity-vr-firm-lays-off-25-focuses-on-virtual-offices, https://ryanschultz.com/2019/12/11/high-fidelity-suspends-its-remote-teamworks-project-announces-more-staff-layoffs-closes-its-open-source-codebase-and-withdraws-its-apps/)

Sale confirmed: Linden Lab press release 24 Mar 2020, Wookey Project Corp (San Francisco) took over all Sansar operations, Tilia retained for payments; Altberg: Sansar 'wasn't making enough money'. Layoffs: Ryan Schultz reported 30 in Nov 2019 (many reshuffled rather than fired), then 40+ in Feb 2020; ~30 staff later got Wookey offers. Concurrency corrected: the phrase 'low hundreds' was not found; community-collected stats show average concurrency 'in the mid two figures for most of the year', a monthly peak of 220 (Sept 2019), and publicly listed experiences rarely above 50 visitors at once. Linden Lab published no Sansar user statistics. Rewrite as: average concurrency in the tens, peaks ~200, per Ryan Schultz/Galen data. (Also: https://modemworld.me/2020/03/24/linden-lab-confirm-the-sale-of-sansar-to-wookey-project-corp/, https://ryanschultz.com/2019/11/04/)

Confirmed: Channel 4 investigation; Balderton wrote its 13% stake down to zero before broadcast; 3i (largest investor) then sold its 16%. Corrections: (a) the closure of all 11 country offices and a 25% workforce cut were announced in February 2012, before the Channel 4 piece, so they are not a consequence of the scandal; (b) October 2012: Sulake announced 'a maximum of 60 out of the 90 jobs will go', negotiations from 5 Nov 2012, CEO Paul LaFontaine citing market competition, so '90 to 30 by October' is an announced ceiling, not a realised headcount; (c) the all-chat mute and the '~75% revenue recovery' did not surface in any extract (mute = widely reported prior knowledge; 75% unverified); (d) US$78.7M 2011 revenue did not surface; extracts give 2008 revenue EUR 50M and a later '$73.6 million with profits of $7 million' (year unclear). LaFontaine left Dec 2012; Markku Ignatius acting CEO Jan 2013. (Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulake, https://arcticstartup.com/?p=48750, https://techcrunch.com/?p=502388)

PRNewswire 25 Jan 2021 (via Nasdaq), PocketGamer.biz and TechCrunch: 'more than $35 million' from Structural Capital, NetEase and others; new parent Together Labs (CEO Daren Tsui); 2020 'over 7 million monthly active users' and 'a record 400,000 products created every month'. All company-reported. TechCrunch adds >$77M raised across five rounds since 2004. A 2024 profile still cites ~7M MAU. (Also: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/imvu-inc-secures-35-million-in-funding, https://techcrunch.com/?p=2099331)

Club NEVERDIE: bought by Jon 'NEVERDIE' Jacobs in 2005 for $100,000 (installed late 2005; Guinness listing 2008), so '(2008)' should read '(bought 2005, Guinness 2008)'; parcels resold for $635,000 total in Nov 2010. Treasure Island: $26,500, Dec 2004, buyer David 'Deathifier' Storey (one source says $27,500). Deposits/withdrawals: MindArk press release 'Metrics of a Virtual World...' is dated 3 January 2025 and states '$242 Million USD in Player Cash Deposits since launch' and '$64 Million USD in Player Cash Withdrawals since launch'; so 'as of 2025' is acceptable if phrased 'Jan 2025 release, cumulative since launch, self-reported' (earlier checker's 'Dec 2024' dating is slightly off). 500,000 users on 17 Oct 2006 not searched (budget); prior knowledge. (Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropia_Universe, https://www.cnbc.com/id/40146233, https://news.cision.com/mindark-pe-ab/r/metrics-of-a-virtual-world-with-boundless-opportunities--discover-the-world-of-entropia-universe,c4087679)

additional_findings: Habbo's contraction preceded the scandal: Sulake announced a 25% workforce cut and closure of all 11 country offices in February 2012, four months before the Channel 4 broadcast; the June 2012 investor exits and the October 2012 plan to cut up to 60 of 90 jobs compounded an existing decline. 'One exposé removed two-thirds of staff' overstates causality; the safer lesson is that a safety scandal is most lethal to a company already shrinking.

Sansar's real engagement was an order of magnitude below 'low hundreds': community-tracked average concurrency in the tens, monthly peak ~220 (Sept 2019), public experiences rarely above 50 visitors. Linden Lab published no stats. Use these as the go/no-go benchmark a successor must clear.

PS Home economics (anecdotal): a developer co-founder said Home was profitable but Sony 'wasn't interested in smaller profit margins' and running/support costs had grown beyond Sony's expectation. Partially answers the open question on profitability; still no Sony figure.

The Sims Online's 105k peak is contested: another account gives ~15,000 active monthly subscribers in 2003. If the lower figure holds, the box-plus-subscription wall failed even harder than the brief says.

MindArk filings: average depositing user deposits >$8,000 over their lifetime; depositors are ~10% of active users; withdrawals carry a 1% fee and a 1,000 PED ($100) minimum. Jan 2025 release also claims six player-run companies on an in-world exchange (combined market cap $25.4M) and 1.5M 'nanotransactions' per hour. All self-reported; useful as a whale-economy reference for a withdrawable-currency design.
Club NEVERDIE parcels resold for $635,000 in Nov 2010 (535% return in five years): scarce, revenue-generating virtual property can appreciate when the currency is withdrawable.
IMVU has raised >$77M across five rounds since 2004; a 2024 profile still cites ~7M MAU, indicating a plateau after the 2021 round rather than growth.

Rosedale's VR miss is framed differently by outlets (Modem World: 10-20M daily HMD users predicted in 2013; VentureBeat: 'millions' predicted in 2014, actual 'tens of thousands'); the ~100x gap holds either way.
Blue Mars' >$13M came mainly from Kolohala Ventures (Hawaii) and co-founder Henk Rogers, i.e. founder-adjacent capital, which likely limited its ability to refinance after the CryEngine bet failed.
There.com's 2012 relaunch included two free-trial tiers alongside the $10/month subscription, so it was not a pure paywall.
Cloud Party's export guide (confirmed) and Sansar's survival through a sale with ~30 staff re-hired are concrete precedents for the brief's 'escrowed sunset plan' implication.

Method limitation: all verdicts rest on search-result extracts; no page could be fetched directly. Unverified by search: High Fidelity's $35M/$73M funding, Entropia's 500k-users date, Habbo's chat mute and 75% revenue recovery, and Sulake's US$78.7M 2011 revenue.
